worksheet.title: Order Matters
worksheet.subtitle: An algorithm is steps in order
worksheet.learning_goal: I can follow steps in order and see where Bit lands.

parts.title: A plan made of steps
parts.text: A plan made of steps in order is called an ALGORITHM. Bit follows the steps one at a time. The arrow ➡ means 'move one box to the right.'

parts.title: Bit's board — Bit starts on box 1
Bit's steps
parts.note: Do the steps in order: first ➡ (box 1 → box 2), then ➡ (box 2 → box 3).

parts.title: One step
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1 and does ➡ one time. Which box is Bit on now? Circle it.   box 1    box 2    box 3

parts.title: Two steps
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1 and does ➡ ➡ (two times). Which box is Bit on now? Circle it.   box 1    box 2    box 3

parts.title: You try — reach the star
parts.prompt: How many ➡ does Bit need to get from box 1 to the star on box 3? Write the number.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: The number of steps decides where Bit lands. Doing the steps in order — one at a time — is how a computer follows an algorithm.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children meet the 1D board and the move arrow ➡, and see that the number of steps decides where Bit lands. This introduces an algorithm as a list of ordered steps carried out one at a time — the spine of the next three sheets.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children carry out a short ordered sequence of moves.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles the landing box and writes a number.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: tape three boxes on the floor and walk Bit's steps.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: point to box 1. 'One ➡ moves Bit to box 2. Another ➡ moves Bit to box 3 — the star.'
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 together — one step lands on box 2.
3. YOU TRY: children do two steps (Ex 2 → box 3), then count the steps to the star (Ex 3 → 2).
4. Connect: 'Doing steps in order, one at a time, is how a computer follows an algorithm.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Model — ➡ ➡ from box 1 lands on box 3 (the star).
Ex 1 — one ➡ → box 2.   Ex 2 — two ➡ → box 3.
Ex 3 — Bit needs 2 steps (➡ ➡) to reach the star on box 3.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: counting the starting box as a move — the first ➡ is the first MOVE from box 1 to box 2.
Simplify: walk the steps on floor boxes before using the page.
Extend: add a box 4 and ask how many steps to reach it (3).
Movement option: children take one step per ➡ you call out and freeze on the landing box.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child lands Bit on the correct box for one and two steps and counts that 2 steps reach the star.
